provenance.what: W11 two-arm A/B: multi-set batch executor vs the per-set walk

arms.plan: shipped: whole-plan occurrence table, one read per file, dedup, exact allocation

provenance.design: one build, two arms selected by environment; arm order alternated by round so neither takes every cold-cache slot; exact two-sided sign test over per-round ratios within a cell
provenance.arms_verified_by: behaviour, per arm, before every timed invocation: four single-shard sets produce 4 block-index request groups under the per-set walk and 1 under the batch executor
provenance.already_measured_elsewhere: the allocation count, by scx-loader/tests/gather_allocation.rs: 2,698 -> 101 for a 1,024-row plan, 2.63 -> 0.10 per row, peak live bytes flat at 421,192 -> 412,480 B
provenance.what_this_is_not: not a consumer-side measurement: R2's data-wait fraction has never been measured, so what this buys a STATE3-class trainer is not answered here
provenance.kept_because: SUPERSEDED, and shipped anyway because it IS the evidence for the fix that supersedes it. At this head the batch executor read a plan's rows through read_row_indices_with_admission, whose indptr prescan re-decoded a RESIDENT shard's indptr on every call. That put the executor at 0.811x on cellsets_per_sec__gather_random (0/12, p=0.000) and 0.820x on __gather_grouped (0/12, p=0.000) -- the two scenarios with no duplicates to amortise it -- while the duplicate-heavy arms still won big (gather_hot_control_cold_tail 7.92x at 12/12, downsample_rust 3.71x at 12/12) and gather_shared_control_per_set came out FLAT (0.975x, 5/12, p=0.774) because the two effects cancelled. The prescan now peeks the shard cache; see the capture beside this one.
